title: What protects expression after CHE-1 depletion?
license: CC BY 4.0; original study and source data credited to Traets et al.
endpoint: gcy-22 mRNA molecules in ASER, measured by smFISH
background: che-1(gj2089[che-1::GFP::AID]); ieSi57 (TIR1), shared by the promoter constructs
treatment: Control versus 24 hours of 1 mM auxin; figure labels early L3

sequence.arm_source: Article Methods: Genomic modifications using CRISPR/Cas9

limitations: Each dot is a supplied workbook observation. Repeated batch and worm labels are preserved; unique animals and independent biological batches are not established.
Control and auxin are unpaired fixed endpoints. Ratios divide group means; they are not within-animal changes. No confidence intervals or population hypothesis tests are inferred from these rows.
Donor/reference alignments reconstruct the intended fully templated product, not sequence-verified final clones.
The fragment transfer changes surrounding sequence, core orientation and target spacing together. This comparison cannot isolate a flank-only or cofactor mechanism.

This panel measures one transcript, not binding affinity, whole neuronal identity, neural activity or prediction of an unseen edit. It is a protective regulatory transfer, not a classical same-background genetic rescue.

source_conflicts.detail: Figure 6F caption names the reciprocal che-1-promoter edit. Main text, figure labels, notebook and donor table instead support the gcy-22 core transfer gj2064. This mapping is our source reconciliation, not an author-issued correction.
Core-transfer sheets have an E1 label naming ASEgcy-22bp, in conflict with A1 and the notebook. Figure 6F selects gcy-22 counts from column C; the unlabelled fragment-auxin column D is not selected.
The native-control sheet labels L3/L4, while Figure 6F labels early L3. The original labels remain unresolved.
Methods specify 0.2% EtOH; Results state 0.25%. Exact solvent metadata is unresolved.
